text.marquee: RANK UP CITY · BUILDING 6 · THE GRAND HOTEL
text.tagline:
Every reply is correct English.
Choose the one that fits.
text.taglineEs: Elige la respuesta justa, corta lo que sobra y brinda contra el reloj. Suma patitas <ico-paw></ico-paw> en cada ronda.
text.help: At the Grand Hotel every reply is correct English. Choose the one that fits the guest: the right word, the right register, the right degree. When the red pen comes out, tap what should go, or tap fine as it is. For the toast, put the parts in order before the time runs out. Need a hint? Lift the silver cover.
text.bossWin: To the guests! And to you. Vera raised her glass and said one word: adequate. From her, that is five stars. You've graduated, A1 to C2, the whole city. The official C2 exam is waiting for you.
text.gameOver: Even the best concierge has a bad night. Take a breath and open the desk again.
text.good: Ms. Whitmore nodded. Once. From her, that's a standing ovation. Your prize is waiting. Claim it!
text.ok: A long night at the desk. Run it back for a better card, or claim your prize anyway.

boss.name: VERA'S FIVE STARS
boss.quote: Adequate. (From her, that is five stars.)

epic.name: MS. WHITMORE
epic.quote: Make it shorter. Make it better.

common.name: MASTER KEY
common.quote: Every door. Use it wisely. Run it back!

hint.name: ENRI
hint.label: LIFT THE COVER
hint.pre: *a muffled purr from under the silver cover*

s1.name: Check-in
s1.intro: Welcome to the Grand Hotel, the summit of the city. You're on the concierge desk with Julian, and the guests here say less than they mean. Every reply is correct English. Choose the one that fits. And if you need a hint, lift the silver cover. Enri lives here now.

rounds.line: The room is… adequate.
rounds.fitNote: Every reply is correct English. Which one hears what she means?
options: I'm sorry to hear it falls short. May I ask what would make it more comfortable?
Thank you! We are very proud of our rooms.
Adequate? It's one of the best rooms we've got.
rounds.retryLine: I said adequate. I chose the word with care.
rounds.thanks: How refreshing. Someone who listens.

rounds.line: The brochure needs one word for our single rooms. They are small. Choose the word a brochure would print.
rounds.fitNote: Same fact, three attitudes. Which one sells the room?
options: Our cozy single rooms…
Our cramped single rooms…
Our poky single rooms…
rounds.retryLine: We are selling the room, not apologizing for it.
rounds.thanks: Cozy. Print it.

rounds.line: The guest in four twelve says the brochure claimed a view of the river.
rounds.note: What does the verb claimed tell you?
options: She doubts the brochure was telling the truth.
She agrees with the brochure.
She wrote the brochure herself.
rounds.retryLine: Claimed is never neutral. Listen to it again.
rounds.thanks: Exactly. From a novelist, that is a complaint.

rounds.line: A guest asks how you are after a double shift. Answer naturally.
rounds.fitNote: All three are grammatical. Which one sounds natural?
options: Absolutely exhausted, but still smiling.
Very exhausted, but still smiling.
Fairly exhausted, but still smiling.
rounds.retryLine: Exhausted is already the top of the scale. Which word goes with it?
rounds.thanks: Absolutely. Go home soon.

rounds.line: Tell the guest, gently, that the suite is not as large as the photographs suggest.
rounds.answer: I'm afraid the suite is somewhat smaller
rounds.retryLine: Gently. I'm afraid, and somewhat.
rounds.thanks: Perfectly judged. Somewhat is doing a great deal of work there.

s2.name: The late arrival
s2.intro: Two in the morning, and a comedian is checking in. Read the room: answer a joke in kind, switch to formal English when the manager walks in, and know when not to joke at all.

rounds.line: Nine dollars for water. Is it famous water?
rounds.fitNote: Every reply is correct English. Answer in kind, and stay professional.
options: It has a very good agent, sir.
The price list is set by the management.
Yeah, it's a total rip-off, isn't it?
rounds.retryLine: Come on. Give me something to work with.
rounds.thanks: Ha! You should be on stage.

rounds.line: Nine hours on the runway. The delay was slightly inconvenient.
rounds.note: What is Rex doing with the word slightly?
options: Understatement: a small word for a big problem.
A pun on two meanings of slightly.
A formal apology.
rounds.retryLine: Nine hours. Slightly. See the gap?
rounds.thanks: Slightly. I'm a professional.

rounds.line: Good morning. Is everything in order?
rounds.fitNote: The manager has walked in. Same message, her register.
options: Good morning, Ms. Whitmore. Our guest has arrived for the summit, and his room is ready.
Hey! The funny guy's here, room's all set.
Yeah, all good. He's in.
rounds.retryLine: I beg your pardon?
rounds.thanks: Excellent. Should he require anything further, you will assist him.

rounds.line: Three apologies for the same lost suitcase. Which one is for the ambassador?
options: I regret to inform you that one item of your luggage has been delayed.
So, bad news: your bag's gone on a little adventure.
I'm so sorry, but your suitcase didn't arrive with the others.
rounds.retryLine: Higher up the ladder. An ambassador.
rounds.thanks: Same suitcase. Three languages, and all of them English.

rounds.line: A guest's flight was canceled, and she has missed her daughter's wedding. She's at the desk.
rounds.fitNote: Is this the moment for a joke?
options: I'm so sorry. Let me see what I can do right away.
Well, look on the bright side: no speeches!
Weddings are overrated anyway.
rounds.retryLine: No. Bad news is never the time.
rounds.thanks: Right. Sometimes the kindest register is the plainest.

s3.name: The symposium
s3.intro: The symposium. Academic English: claim exactly as much as the evidence allows, spot the argument that cheats, and choose your citing verb with care.

rounds.line: The bulletin needs one sentence on Dr. Lane's study. Three hundred adults, two years.
rounds.fitNote: All three are grammatical. Which one claims what the study allows?
options: Her study suggests that learners make more local friends.
Her study proves that learners make more local friends.
Her study shows beyond doubt that tools ruin friendships.
rounds.retryLine: One study. Small sample. How strong can the verb be?
rounds.thanks: Suggests. Dr. Lane would approve.

rounds.line: Two questions from the floor. Which one attacks a position I never took?
options: So you want us to throw our phones away?
Did you measure how sociable people were before the study?
Would the result hold for children?
rounds.retryLine: One of them is a fair question. Find the one that isn't.
rounds.thanks: A straw man. I cannot defend a position I do not hold.

rounds.line: Introduce the limit of my study without owning the idea yourself.
rounds.answer: It could be argued that the evidence is limited
rounds.retryLine: It could be argued that. The passive keeps you neutral.
rounds.thanks: Precisely. And it is, to some extent.

rounds.line: Introduce Dr. Lane's main point for the bulletin. She argues it firmly; you stay neutral.
rounds.fitNote: The citing verb carries a verdict. Which one is neutral?
options: Dr. Lane contends that machines cannot build trust.
Dr. Lane admits that machines cannot build trust.
Dr. Lane claims, wrongly, that machines cannot build trust.
rounds.retryLine: Admits blames her. Claims doubts her. Neither is neutral.
rounds.thanks: Contends. Neutral, and accurate.

rounds.line: Last one. Which of these sentences states a limit?
options: These findings are limited to adults in three cities.
Taken together, the studies point one way.
This raises the question of motivation.
rounds.retryLine: A limit says where the claim stops.
rounds.thanks: Exactly. Further research is needed. As we always say.

s4.name: The critic's suite
s4.intro: The critic's suite. Vera speaks in images, so keep her metaphors whole. Then Ms. Whitmore hands you the red pen: cut what should go.

rounds.line: The first chapter simmers.
options: Mostly: it is slow, and promising.
No: she thinks it is burnt.
She is talking about the soup.
rounds.retryLine: Simmering is patient cooking, darling. Is that bad?
rounds.thanks: Mostly. Patience is not a crime. Yet.

rounds.line: But the second half never comes to the boil.
rounds.fitNote: Stay in her kitchen. Which reply keeps the image whole?
options: Perhaps the author turned the heat down on purpose.
Perhaps the train left the rails there.
Perhaps it hits a home run later.
rounds.retryLine: A train? In my kitchen?
rounds.thanks: Hm. Perhaps she did. A point to you.

rounds.line: The welcome card. One word is doing no work. Remove it.
rounds.text: Every guest will receive a free gift at the door.
rounds.fix: Every guest will receive a gift at the door.
rounds.retryLine: No. Which word is a gift by definition?
rounds.thanks: Tighter. Thank you.

rounds.line: And this sentence. Something in it is attached to the wrong thing.
rounds.fix: Walking into the ballroom, every guest was dazzled by the chandelier.
rounds.retryLine: Who was walking? Not the chandelier.
rounds.thanks: Quite. Chandeliers do not walk. Not in my hotel.

rounds.line: The card ends: In conclusion, I would like to express the hope that you will enjoy the evening. Three words, please.
rounds.retryLine: Three words. A short sentence after long ones.
rounds.thanks: Enjoy the evening. I did not say it was worse.

sb.name: The gala
sb.intro: The gala. Ms. Whitmore has lost her voice, and the toast is yours. Thank, story, wish, against the clock, and every guest wants a word on the way to the stage. Do it, and you graduate. A1 to C2. The whole city.

rounds.line: Ms. Whitmore has lost her voice. The toast is yours. Put it in order.
parts: Thank you all for three remarkable days.
On Friday, a novelist called her room adequate. Tonight she asked to stay until Wednesday.
May you all travel home safely, and come back soon.
rounds.retryLine: Thank them first. Then the story. Then the wish.
rounds.thanks: That's the shape. Now say it like you mean it.

rounds.line: And what, exactly, will you say in your toast?
options: That's a very good question. Ask me again in an hour.
I don't know. I'm very nervous. Sorry.
Things about the hotel and the guests.
rounds.retryLine: Darling. Again, with poise.
rounds.thanks: Hm. I shall.

rounds.line: Before you go up. I need something to open this bottle.
rounds.fitNote: You've lost the word. Keep talking.
options: Of course. You need a, what's the word, the thing you use to pull the cork. I'll send one up.
You need a… sorry. I forgot the word. Sorry.
Yes. Bottles need to be opened.
rounds.retryLine: Don't stop. Describe it.
rounds.thanks: A corkscrew. You found it without finding it. I'll put that in the book.

rounds.line: Your card, on the way to the stage. One phrase breaks the pattern.
rounds.text: Thank you all for coming, for listening and for having laughed.
rounds.fix: Thank you all for coming, for listening and for laughing.
rounds.retryLine: Coming, listening… and the third one?
rounds.thanks: Parallel. Go.

rounds.line: The final toast. The room is waiting. Thirty seconds.
parts: This weekend, two hundred stories walked through our door.
May every one of them have a happy ending.
rounds.retryLine: Thank. Story. Wish. Glass.
rounds.thanks: To the summit. Well done.
